title: Urban Heat Islands

segments.say: Myth: a city is hot only because of the weather. Fact: the city itself makes some of that heat.
On the same day, a city centre is often warmer than the fields around it. That warm patch is called an urban heat island.

anim.title: Why cities run hot
items: Roads and roofs soak up sunlight
They give off heat after sunset
Few trees to shade and cool
Vehicles and air conditioners add waste heat

segments.say: Roads and roofs absorb more of the Sun's heat than trees and soil do, and give it off after sunset. Vehicles and air conditioners add even more.
Trees and lakes do the opposite. They give shade, and cool the air as water evaporates from leaves and ponds.
In American studies, cities ran up to about seven degrees Fahrenheit warmer by day, and up to five at night. Warmer nights give the body less relief.
The fixes are simple to name: more trees, green roofs or light-coloured roofs, and pavements that reflect sunlight instead of storing it.
For GS One, link this to urbanisation: how we build a city changes its climate. Quote one cause and one fix.

sources: US EPA, 'Learn About Heat Islands': urban areas about 1–7°F warmer by day and 2–5°F warmer at night than outlying areas (US studies); pavements and roofing absorb and emit more of the Sun's heat; trees, vegetation and water bodies cool through shade, transpiration and evaporation; human-generated waste heat adds to it
US EPA Heat Island Reduction Solutions pages: trees and vegetation, green roofs, cool roofs, cool pavements

quiz.q: What is an urban heat island?
options: An island city in the sea
A city area warmer than its surroundings
quiz.why: Cities are often warmer than the countryside around them.

quiz.q: Which of these cools a city?
quiz.why: Trees and water cool the air by shade, transpiration and evaporation.

quiz.q: Which of these is a cause of heat islands?
options: Roads and roofs storing the Sun's heat
quiz.why: Built surfaces absorb more heat and release it after sunset.

reviewNote: Facts were read against the US EPA heat island pages. The temperature figures are from US studies and are labelled that way on screen; no Indian city figure is claimed. The bars diagram uses the top of each range. Moving facts: none known.
